[[CBE Hall of Fame Classic]] champions |bowl = [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Elite Eight }} {{2016–17 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kansas]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], which was the Jayhawks' 119th basketball season. The Jayhawks, members of the [[Big 12 Conference]], played their home games at [[Allen Fieldhouse]] and were led by 14th-year head coach [[Bill Self]]. They finished the season 31–5, 16–2 in Big 12 play to win their 13th consecutive Big 12 regular season title, tying [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]'s record for consecutive regular season conference titles.{{cite web|title=No. 3 Kansas routs TCU 87-68 to clinch share of Big 12 title|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400916252|website=ESPN.com}} They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2017 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] to [[2016–17 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 1 seed in the Midwest region. This was their 28th consecutive appearance, the longest active streak at the time and the longest ever in NCAA Tournament history.{{Cite web|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2017/mar/13/jayhawks-set-all-time-mark-28th-consecutive-ncaa-t/|title=Jayhawks set all-time mark with 28th consecutive NCAA Tournament appearance|website=KUsports.com|language=en|access-date=2017-06-02}} It was the final official appearance in the streak as their tournament appearance in the following season was vacated by the NCAA. In the Tturnament, they defeated [[2016–17 UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team|UC Davis]] and [[2016–17 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. There they defeated [[2016–17 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] before losing in the Elite Eight to [[2016–17 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]]. The Jayhawks entered the season with 40 straight wins at Allen Fieldhouse, which extended to 51 games during the season before it ended on February 5, 2017, with an 92–89 loss to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], which was the longest active home arena winning streak in the nation when it ended.{{Cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/kansas-iowa-state-final-stats-scores-details-video-home-court-win-streak-snapped-020417|title=Kansas' 54-game home winning streak ends in stunning upset {{!}} FOX Sports|date=2017-02-04|work=FOX Sports|access-date=2017-06-02|language=en-US}}{{Cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/kansas-shocked-by-unranked-iowa-state-in-overtime-after-two-straight-top-10-wins-212556009.html|title=No. 3 Kansas shocked by unranked Iowa State, ending nation's longest home win streak|access-date=2017-06-02|language=en-US}} ==Preseason== ===Departures=== ====Graduation==== {| class="wikitable" !
